entries.title: Proverbs 26:1
segments: ¶Like snow in summer and rain when the grain is being cut, so honour is not natural for the foolish.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:2
segments: ¶As the sparrow in her wandering and the swallow in her flight, so the curse does not come without a cause.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:3
segments: ¶A whip for the horse, a mouth-bit for the ass, and a rod for the back of the foolish.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:4
segments: ¶Do not give to the foolish man a foolish answer, or you will be like him.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:5
segments: Give a foolish man a foolish answer, or he will seem wise to himself.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:6
segments: ¶He who sends news by the hand of a foolish man is cutting off his feet and drinking in damage.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:7
segments: The legs of one who has no power of walking are hanging loose; so is a wise saying in the mouth of the foolish.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:8
segments: Giving honour to a foolish man is like attempting to keep a stone fixed in a cord.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:9
segments: Like a thorn which goes up into the hand of a man overcome by drink, so is a wise saying in the mouth of a foolish man.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:10
segments: ¶Like an archer wounding all who go by, is a foolish man overcome by drink.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:11
segments: ¶Like a dog going back to the food which he has not been able to keep down, is the foolish man doing his foolish acts over again.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:12
segments: ¶Have you seen a man who seems to himself to be wise? There is more hope for the foolish than for him.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:13
segments: ¶The hater of work says, There is a lion in the way; a lion is in the streets.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:14
segments: ¶A door is turned on its pillar, and the hater of work on his bed.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:15
segments: ¶The hater of work puts his hand deep into the basin: lifting it again to his mouth is a weariness to him.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:16
segments: ¶The hater of work seems to himself wiser than seven men who are able to give an answer with good sense.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:17
segments: ¶He who gets mixed up in a fight which is not his business, is like one who takes a dog by the ears while it is going by.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:18
segments: ¶As one who is off his head sends about flaming sticks and arrows of death,

entries.title: Proverbs 26:19
segments: So is the man who gets the better of his neighbour by deceit, and says, Am I not doing so in sport?

entries.title: Proverbs 26:20
segments: ¶Without wood, the fire goes out; and where there is no secret talk, argument is ended.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:21
segments: Like breath on coals and wood on fire, so a man given to argument gets a fight started.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:22
segments: The words of one who says evil of his neighbour secretly are like sweet food, they go down into the inner parts of the stomach.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:23
segments: ¶Smooth lips and an evil heart are like a vessel of earth plated with silver waste.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:24
segments: ¶With his lips the hater makes things seem what they are not, but deceit is stored up inside him;

entries.title: Proverbs 26:25
segments: When he says fair words, have no belief in him; for in his heart are seven evils:

entries.title: Proverbs 26:26
segments: Though his hate is covered with deceit, his sin will be seen openly before the meeting of the people.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:27
segments: ¶He who makes a hole in the earth will himself go falling into it: and on him by whom a stone is rolled the stone will come back again.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:28
segments: ¶A false tongue has hate for those who have clean hearts, and a smooth mouth is a cause of falling.
